units.title: Attention is quadratic; fast alternatives are weak on text
units.summary: Transformers scale quadratically with context length. Structured state space models (SSMs) scale linearly but have done poorly on discrete, information-dense data such as language.

claims.text: Attention scales quadratically with the window length.

refs.quote: quadratic scaling with respect to the window length

claims.text: Prior SSMs were less effective on text.

refs.quote: they have been less effective at modeling discrete and information-dense data such as text
quadratic scaling with respect to the window length
they have been less effective at modeling discrete and information-dense data such as text

units.title: Selection: make the SSM's parameters depend on the input
units.summary: Letting Δ, B and C be functions of the current token lets the model decide, token by token, what to keep in its fixed-size state and what to forget.

claims.text: The SSM parameters become functions of the input.

refs.quote: simply letting the SSM parameters be functions of the input

claims.text: This lets the model filter out irrelevant information and remember relevant information.

refs.quote: This allows the model to filter out irrelevant information and remember relevant information indefinitely.
simply letting the SSM parameters be functions of the input

units.title: A hardware-aware scan keeps it fast
units.summary: Input-dependent parameters rule out the convolution trick, so Mamba runs a parallel scan that keeps the expanded state in fast GPU SRAM instead of HBM.

claims.text: The expanded state is not materialized in slow GPU memory.

refs.quote: does not materialize the expanded state in order to avoid IO access between different levels of the GPU memory hierarchy
perform the discretization and recurrence in SRAM

claims.text: Up to 3× faster than previous methods on A100 GPUs; 4–5× higher inference throughput than a Transformer of similar size.

units.title: Selection solves tasks fixed SSMs cannot
units.summary: On Selective Copying, swapping S4 for the selective S6 layer lifts accuracy from 18.3% to 97.0%; Mamba with S6 reaches 99.8%. On induction heads it extrapolates to 4000× the training length.

claims.text: Selective Copying accuracy: S4 18.3%, S6 97.0%, Mamba+S6 99.8%.

claims.text: Induction heads: perfect up to 4000× the training length.

units.title: Matches Transformers twice its size on language
units.summary: In zero-shot evaluations Mamba-2.8B averages 63.3, above Pythia-2.8B (59.1) and Pythia-6.9B (61.7), all trained on the same data and tokenizer.

units.title: What the paper does not show
units.summary: Results stop at about 3B parameters; selection can hurt on continuous signals; and the Transformer ecosystem (fine-tuning, RLHF, quantization) is untested.

claims.text: The evaluation is limited to small model sizes.

refs.quote: Our empirical evaluation is limited to small model sizes

claims.text: Selection can impede performance where LTI SSMs excel.

claims.text: Whether later work confirmed these results at larger scale is outside this paper.
